priceNote: Ontario-stamped shelf/online prices observed Aug–Sep 2026 across Toronto retailers, before 13% HST. Prices vary by flavour and store.

products.name: STLTH x Geek Bar 80K
products.flavourExamples: Blue Razz, Banana Burst Ice, Juicy Peach Ice, Mango Peach Ice, Strawberry Kiwi Ice, Blueberry Watermelon Ice, Coconut Ice, Rich Tobacco
pros: 30 mL from Canada's most-trusted vape brand
Pulse mode for a stronger hit on demand
Stocked by virtually every Toronto shop
cons: 820 mAh battery is smaller than 1000 mAh rivals — charge every ~2 days
products.verdict: The consensus pick across every source we checked. STLTH's Toronto-based QA plus Geek Bar's hardware make this the safest 30 mL buy in the city. If you only read one line: buy this.

products.name: STLTH Titan Max 50K
products.puffsNote: Same 30 mL as the 80K devices — rated at higher output
products.flavourExamples: Honeydew Ice (fan favourite), Banana Ice, Blue Razz Ice, Mango Ice, Strawberry Ice, Watermelon Ice, Tobacco
products.award: Best value from a trusted brand
pros: Identical 30 mL to the 80K class, frequently $5–10 cheaper
Nearly two years on the market; strong reliability record
cons: '50K' label makes buyers think it's smaller (it isn't)
No Eco mode — uses liquid faster than Eco-rated rivals
products.verdict: The market's best-kept secret. The '50K' number makes it look inferior to '80K' devices, but it holds exactly the same 30 mL and often costs less. If you'd run Boost mode anyway, this is the smarter STLTH.

products.name: Flavour Beast Alpha 80K
products.coil: Physical coil switching: 1.0Ω single mesh (L1–2) / 0.5Ω dual mesh (L3–4)
products.flavourExamples: Extreme Mint Iced, Bomb Blue Razz, Meta Melon Citrus Iced, Jumpin' Juicy Peach, Supreme Strawberry Kiwi, Fruity G candy series
pros: Only disposable that physically switches coils
Flavour Beast recipes are the boldest in Canada
cons: 850 mAh is small for 23 W use
products.verdict: If flavour intensity and control matter more than $5, this is the one. Run Level 1–2 all day and Level 4 when you want a show. Budget for it.

products.name: Rocky Vapor Oxbar G100K
products.flavourExamples: Blueberry Raspberry, Cherry Watermelon, Fresh Mint, Grape Ice, M.D.W. (lemon-lime), Peach Berry, Raspberry Lemon, Watermelon Ice
pros: Less sugary profiles than Flavour Beast
cons: '100K' is marketing — same 30 mL as the 80K devices
Newer to Toronto shelves; fewer long-term reports
products.verdict: Best hardware per dollar among all-in-one disposables. Ignore the 100K number; buy it because it's a 1000 mAh, three-mode, 30 mL device for $42.

products.name: Vice Box 2 70K
products.flavourExamples: Rage Ice, Blue Razz Burst, Frosty Green Apple, Mango Tango Ice, Strawberry Kiwi Ice, Arctic Blue Lemon, Lush Ice
pros: Lowest $/mL of any 30 mL disposable in Toronto
Adjustable airflow + screen at a budget price
cons: Single coil — flavour thins toward the end
Multiple user reports of leaks/duds over the years
products.verdict: The price leader, and fine if you get a good unit. Test-fire it in store. For $3–4 more, the Oxbar G100K or Titan Max is a clear upgrade.

products.name: Elf Bar BC Pro 80K
products.flavourExamples: Strawberry Kiwi Ice (#1 seller), Blue Razz Ice, Blueberry Sour Raspberry, Miami Mint, Kiwi Guava Ice, Double Mango
pros: Only device where you can SEE the remaining liquid
Cheapest entry into the big class ($32–39 typical)
Elf Bar coils are consistently smooth
cons: No screen, no modes, fixed airflow
Huge price spread by flavour and store
products.verdict: A pragmatic pick: the transparent tank ends the 'is it empty or is my battery dead?' guessing game. Shop around — the same device ranges from $32 to $44 across Toronto.

products.name: STLTH 60K
products.flavourExamples: Blue Razz, Mango, Peach Ice, Watermelon Ice, Mint, Tobacco
pros: Retailers report the highest repurchase rate
cons: Overshadowed by the Geek Bar collab
products.verdict: The 'boring but reliable' STLTH. Good if you want modes and a slightly smaller body than Titan Max — but compare the price against the 80K.

products.name: Flavour Beast Beast Mode Max 2
products.flavourExamples: Trippin' Triple Berry, Bangin' Blood Orange, Mangabeys Iced, Tropika Iced, Kanzi Iced, Mad Mango Peach, Wild White Grape
pros: Top revenue seller in Canada — flavours people love
Same pod format as Level X G2 (buy the battery later and switch to pods)
cons: One documented DOA on Reddit (manufacturer replaced it)
products.verdict: Great flavours, weak value. If you like Flavour Beast, step up to the Alpha or sideways to a Level X G2 battery + Ultra pods for far less per mL.

products.name: Geek Bar Pulse X 25K
products.flavourExamples: Blue Razz Ice, Miami Mint, Strawberry B-Pop, Watermelon Ice, Sour Apple Ice, Grape Blow Pop, Tobacco
pros: Widely considered the best-tasting disposable line
Proven since 2024; Pulse 2 successor now out
cons: 18 mL — heavy users empty it in a week
products.verdict: If 30 mL bricks are too big for your pocket, this is the one to carry. Pay a bit more per mL for the best flavour tech in the mid class.

products.name: WAKA DUO 28000
products.flavourExamples: Cuke Lemon Lime Ice, Grapefruit Lime Ice, Canada D. Ice, Blue Razz Ice, Watermelon Ice
cons: Ontario price is steep for ~18 mL
products.verdict: For adults who find most disposables sickly sweet. Cuke Lemon Lime Ice is unlike anything else on Toronto shelves.

products.name: Infinity Lean 20K
products.flavourExamples: Blue Razz Lemon Ice (top), Watermelon Ice, Mango Peach, Extreme Mint
pros: Top unit-seller at its retailer (1,350 in 6 months)
products.verdict: The lowest-stakes way to try a disposable in Toronto. Not fancy; just cheap and decent.

products.name: Elf Bar GH 20K
products.flavourExamples: Tropical fruits, creamy desserts, icy menthols
pros: Broad flavour range incl. dessert profiles
products.verdict: A solid, no-frills mid-sizer. Only buy at the low end of its price range.

products.name: Oxbar G42K
products.flavourExamples: Fruit ice range
pros: World-first adjustable nicotine output — lets you taper
products.verdict: Buy this for the nicotine dial, not the value. It's the only disposable that lets a daily user actually cut intake without switching devices.

products.name: STLTH Loop Max (device + 30 mL pods)
products.coil: Mesh — fresh coil in every pod
products.flavourExamples: Razz Apple Ice, Blue Razz, Mango, Peach Ice, Watermelon Ice, Mint
pros: ~$0.90–1.20/mL — cheapest legit nicotine per mL in Toronto
New coil with every pod — no end-of-life metallic taste
Far less e-waste than binning a 1000 mAh cell each time
cons: Two-part system: carry the right pod
Pods only fit Loop Max (not Loop 2/3)
products.verdict: If you're a daily user spending $45 every week or two, do the math: this pays for itself on the first pod. Same STLTH liquid, same 30 mL, half the waste.

products.name: Level X G2 + Ultra 50K pods
products.flavourExamples: Flavour Beast lineup + Drip'n (Canada D Ice) + Unleashed series (Epic Grape Iced)
products.priceNote: per 20 mL pod; G2 battery ~$15–25 one-time
products.award: Best hybrid for Flavour Beast fans
pros: Flavour Beast flavours at ~$1.25–1.70/mL instead of $2–2.50
Beast Mode Max 2 pods also fit
Biggest flavour catalogue of any system
cons: 20 mL pods — swap more often than Loop Max
G2 Pro battery only fits G2 pods (check compatibility)
products.verdict: The obvious move for anyone buying Beast Mode Max 2 disposables on repeat.

products.name: Allo Ultra 2500
products.flavourExamples: 30+ incl. Classic Tobacco, Mint, Blue Raspberry, Mango, Lychee Ice
pros: Zero learning curve — no buttons, no charging
1500 mAh never dies before the liquid
Tobacco/mint versions at some convenience stores
cons: ~$2.90/mL — more than double the ultra class
Non-rechargeable = whole 1500 mAh cell in the bin
products.verdict: Right for occasional or travel use. Wrong for a daily user's wallet.

products.name: Vuse Go 8000 (2.0)
products.flavourExamples: Mint Ice, Menthol, Tobacco (c-store); Strawberry Ice, Mango, Berry Blend (specialty only)
products.award: Best you can buy at a convenience store
pros: At gas stations and c-stores across Toronto (mint/menthol/tobacco only)
Big Tobacco QA and recall accountability
cons: Flavour is flat next to specialty brands
products.verdict: The 11 pm emergency option when every vape shop is closed. Otherwise, walk the extra block.

products.name: Kraze Giga 150K
products.flavourExamples: RAZ-style fruit ice range
pros: 40 mL — the largest tank sold in Canada
Kraze = Canadian arm of RAZ, a known quantity
cons: Brand-new; few people have finished one
One coil across 40 mL — end-of-life taste is a real concern
800 mg of nicotine in your hand
products.verdict: Wait for reports. On paper it's the value king; in practice a single coil running 40 mL is an experiment you're paying $50 to join.

products.name: Orbito Lumo AI 120K
products.flavourExamples: Fruit ice range
pros: Available in 10 mg/mL — half strength — rare in Canada
cons: '120K' from 30 mL is the most inflated claim on the shelf
Premium price for no track record
products.verdict: Interesting only for the 10 mg version if you're tapering. Otherwise unproven.

products.name: Mr. Fog Aura 60K
products.flavourExamples: Fruit ice range
products.verdict: A credible local option if your shop stocks it; verify the mL on the box before paying 80K-class money.
